body.text: karmavastu
body.translated_text: <s>Karmavastu</s> (Section on Legal Procedures)

children.translated_text: In <s>Campā</s>, the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> should reject invalid legal acts.

body.text: kāśiṣu vāsavagrāmake senāṃjayo nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tam āgamya vāsavagrāmakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu kārān kurvanti / ye āgantukā bhikṣavo vāsavagrāmakam āgacchanti tān asau pratiśāmya sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayitvā mārgaśrame prativinodite yeṣu kuleṣu piṇḍakā upanibaddhās teṣu bhoktuṃ preṣayati / yāvad anyatamaḥ sālohito vāsavagrāmake varṣā uṣitaḥ / trayāṇāṃ vārṣikāṇāṃ māsānām atyayāt kṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ samādāya pātracīvaraṃ yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrānto 'nupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caran śrāvastīṃ anuprāptaḥ /
body.translated_text: In <s>Kāśī</s>, in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, a monk named <s>Senāṃjaya</s> was residing. On account of him, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s> performed services for the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. Whenever visiting monks came to <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, he would receive them, offer them all requisites, and once their travel fatigue was relieved, he would send them to eat at those families where alms-food was arranged for monks. Then a certain blood-relative, having spent the rainy season in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, after the three months of the rains had passed, having made his robe and completed his robe-work, taking his bowl and robe, set out wandering toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and wandering gradually, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text: ācaritaṃ ṣaḍvargikāṇām aśūnyaṃ jetavanadvāram anyatarānyatareṇa ṣaḍvargikeṇa / upanando jetavanadvāre tiṣṭhati / tenāsau dūrata eva dṛṣṭo bakākāraśirāḥ pralambabhrūḥ / sa saṃlakṣayati / ko 'py ayaṃ sthaviro bhikṣur āgacchati / pratyudgantavyam iti / sa pratyudgataḥ / svāgataṃ svāgataṃ sthavira iti / sa kathayati / vande ācārya iti / sa saṃlakṣayati / mahallo batāyam* / nāyam ācāryaṃ jānīte nāpy upādhyāyam iti / sālohita kiyad dūrād āgacchasi / vāsavagrāmakāt* / kiṃ tatra / vihāraḥ / kim asau vihāraḥ / āhosvid (

children.text: ) vighātaḥ / kīdṛśo vihāraḥ / kīdṛśo vighātaḥ / yatropakaraṇasaṃpat sa vihāraḥ / yatropakaraṇavaikalyaṃ sa vighātaḥ / yady evaṃ vihāro 'sau yatra senāṃjayo nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tam āgamya vāsavagrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu kārān kurvanti / itaś ca tatrāgantuko bhikṣur āgacchati / tam asau pratiśāmya sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayitvā mārgaśrame prativinodite yeṣu kuleṣu bhikṣūṇāṃ piṇḍakā upanibaddhās teṣu bhoktuṃ preṣayati /
children.translated_text: ) or a ruin? What kind of monastery? What kind of ruin?" "Where there is abundance of requisites, that is a monastery. Where there is lack of requisites, that is a ruin." "If so, that is indeed a monastery, where a monk named <s>Senāṃjaya</s> resides. On account of him, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s> perform services for the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. And when a visiting monk comes there, he receives him, offers him all requisites, and once travel fatigue is relieved, sends him to eat at those families where alms-food is arranged for monks."

body.translated_text: It was the custom of the Group of Six that the gate of <s>Jetavana</s> was never empty of one or another of the Group of Six. <s>Upananda</s> was standing at the gate of <s>Jetavana</s>. He saw that one from afar — with a head shaped like a crane's and drooping eyebrows. He thought: "Some elder monk is coming. I should go out to meet him." He went out to meet him. "Welcome, welcome, elder!" The other said: "I pay respects, teacher." He thought: "This one is indeed old! He does not know his teacher nor his preceptor." "Friend, from how far have you come?" "From <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>." "What is there?" "A monastery." "Is that a monastery (

body.text: ācaritaṃ ṣaḍvargikāṇāṃ yat kiṃcid eva śṛṇvanti tad rātrau saṃnipatya parasparam ārocayanti / nandopananda kiyac ciram asmābhiḥ kṛcchram udvoḍhavyam* / asti kiṃcid yuṣmākaṃ kiṃcic chrutaṃ yatrodārāvabhāso bhaved iti / upanandaḥ kathayati / asti / kāśiṣu vāsavagrāmake senāṃjayo nāma bhikṣuḥ prativasati / tam āgamya vāsavagrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ pūrvavad yāvad bhoktuṃ preṣayati / yady abhipretaṃ tatra gacchāmaḥ / te samādāya pātracīvaraṃ yena vāsavagrāmakas tena cārikāṃ prakrāntāḥ / anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caranto vāsavagrāmakam anuprāptāḥ / te senāṃjayena dūrata eva dṛṣṭāḥ / sa saṃlakṣayati / āgatā hy ete duṣṭhulasamudācārāḥ / pratiśāmayitvā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayitavyāḥ / no tu kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣayitavyā iti / te anena pratiśāmayitvā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritāḥ / no tu kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣitāḥ / teṣām eke kathayanti / nandopananda vayam anena mahallena sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravāritāḥ / no tu kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣitā iti / apare kathayanti / ekaṃ tāvat saṃpannaṃ kulāny api (

children.text: ) yāvan navako bhikṣur āgataḥ / sa tena pratiśāmayitvā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārito mārgaśrame prativinodite kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣitaḥ / ṣaḍvargikāḥ prakupitāḥ kathayanti / nandopananda kīdṛśo 'yaṃ
children.translated_text: ) Then a junior monk arrived. <s>Senāṃjaya</s> received him, offered him all requisites, and once his travel fatigue was relieved, sent him to families to eat. The Group of Six became angry and said: "<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, what kind of old man is this,

children.text: chandadveṣī / yadi tāvat pūrvam āgatās te vayam* /
children.translated_text: acting with partiality! If it is about who arrived first, that is us.
If it is about who is senior, that is us.

children.text: atha bahuśrutās te vayam* / eṣa bhikṣur acireṇābhyāgato navakaḥ prakṛtijñaḥ / so 'nena sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayitvā kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣito no tu vayam* / sa tair upālabdhaḥ / mahalla īdṛśas tvaṃ chandadveṣī / yadi tāvat pūrvam āgatās te vayaṃ pūrvavad yāvat* / sa tvayā sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pravārayitvā kulāni bhoktuṃ preṣito no tu vayam* / sthavirā kiṃcit parihīyate / ṣaḍvargikāḥ saṃjātāmarṣāḥ kathayanti / na tūṣṇīṃ sthātavyam* / tad aparaṃ prativadati / sa tair abhyāhataḥ / tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ / tais tasyācodayitvāsmārayitvā vastukarmapratijñāyā balād utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karmaṃ kṛtam* / sa saṃlakṣayati / duḥkhaṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ prasādyante sukham aprasādyante / yadi sthāsyāmi vāsavagrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ prasādaṃ pravedayiṣyante / sarvadā prakramitavyam iti / sa samādāya pātracīvaraṃ yena śrāvastī yena cārikāṃ prakrānto 'nupūrveṇa cārikāṃ (
children.translated_text: Now, "we are the learned ones. This <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) has recently arrived, a newcomer, knowing the local customs. He, having been invited with all requisites by that [senior monk], was sent to eat at the [lay] families — but not us." He was reproached by them: "O elder, you are such a partisan (<s>chandadveṣin</s>)! We came first, [and should be treated] as before." He, having been invited by you with all requisites, was sent to eat at the families — but not us. The elder fell somewhat short [in his response]. The monks of the group of six (<s>ṣaḍvargika</s>), having become angry, said: "One should not remain silent." He replied further. He was struck by them. He remained silent. By them, without admonishing or reminding him, without [proper] commitment to the matter and procedure, the act of suspension (<s>utkṣepaṇīya karma</s>) was forcibly performed against him. He reflected: "The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders are difficult to please and easy to displease. If I stay, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Vāsavagrāma</s> will lose their faith. I should depart at all events." Taking his bowl and robe, he set out on a journey toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and traveling by stages on his journey,

children.text: ) caran śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ / sa bhikṣubhir dṛṣṭa uktaś ca / svāgataṃ svāgatam āyuṣman* / senāñjayin prītā vayaṃ tvaddarśanena no tv āgamanena / kiṃ kāraṇam* / tvām āgamya vāsavagrāmīyakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhadharmasaṃgheṣu kārān kurvanti / āgantukānāṃ gamikānāṃ ca vāsavagrāmakaṃ pratiśaraṇam* / asty etad evam* / mama tu ṣaḍvargikair acodayitvāsmārayitvā vastukarmapratijñāyā balād utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kṛtam / kiṃ kāraṇam* / tena yathāvṛttam ākhyātam* / te 'vadhyāyantaḥ kṣipanto vivācayanta etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo vyagreṇa na bhikṣubhir acodayitvāsmārayitvā vastukarmapratijñayā balād utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kartavyam* / kurvanti / sātisārā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: he arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He was seen by the <s>bhikṣus</s>, who said: "Welcome, welcome, venerable <s>Senāñjayin</s>! We are pleased by seeing you, but not by your coming. Why? Owing to your [presence], the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Vāsavagrāma</s> perform services for the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>. <s>Vāsavagrāma</s> is a refuge for visiting and departing [monks]." "That is indeed so. But the act of suspension was forcibly performed against me by the monks of the group of six, without admonishing or reminding me, without [proper] commitment to the matter and procedure." "Why?" He narrated what had happened. They, disapproving, criticizing, and rebuking, reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, <s>bhikṣus</s>, when the assembly is incomplete (<s>vyagra</s>), the <s>bhikṣus</s> should not perform the act of suspension forcibly without admonishing, without reminding, without [proper] commitment to the matter and procedure. If they do, they commit a transgression (<s>sātisāra</s>)."

body.translated_text: It was the custom of the Group of Six that whatever they heard, they would gather at night and report to one another. "<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, how long must we endure hardship? Have you heard of anything where there might be a prospect of abundance?" <s>Upananda</s> said: "There is. In <s>Kāśī</s>, in <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>, a monk named <s>Senāṃjaya</s> resides. On account of him, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> householders of <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>... as before... sends them to eat. If you agree, let us go there." Taking their bowls and robes, they set out wandering toward <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. Wandering gradually, they arrived at <s>Vāsavagrāmaka</s>. <s>Senāṃjaya</s> saw them from afar. He thought: "These ones of bad conduct have come. They must be received and offered all requisites, but they should not be sent to families to eat." He received them and offered them all requisites, but did not send them to families to eat. Some of them said: "<s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upananda</s>, we have been offered all requisites by this old one, but not sent to families to eat." Others said: "One thing at least has been accomplished; he will send us to families too (

body.text: buddho bhagavān caṇpāyāṃ viharati gargāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre / tena khalu samayena ṣaḍvargikā bhikṣava imāny evaṃrūpāṇy adharmakarmāṇi kurvanti / tadyathā adharmeṇa kurvanti vyagrāḥ / adharmeṇa kurvanti samagrāḥ / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / tasmān na bhikṣubhir imāny evaṃrūpāṇy adharmakarmāṇi karaṇīyāni / tadyathā adharmeṇa vyagrair adharmeṇa samagraiḥ dharmeṇa vyagraiḥ / kurvanti / sātisārā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, was dwelling at <s>Campā</s>, on the bank of <s>Gargā</s>'s lotus pond. At that time, the monks of the group of six (<s>ṣaḍvargika</s>) performed these kinds of illegitimate acts (<s>adharmakarmāṇi</s>): namely, they performed [acts] contrary to the <s>Dharma</s> with an incomplete assembly (<s>vyagra</s>); they performed [acts] contrary to the <s>Dharma</s> with a complete assembly (<s>samagra</s>). The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, <s>bhikṣus</s> should not perform these kinds of illegitimate acts: namely, contrary to the <s>Dharma</s> with an incomplete assembly, contrary to the <s>Dharma</s> with a complete assembly, or in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s> with an incomplete assembly. If they do, they commit a transgression."

body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

body.text: na eka ekena

dvau na saṃbahulāḥ kṛtāḥ /
na gaṇo gaṇasya karmāṇi paṃca saṃghakarmaṇāṃ svāminaḥ //
children.translated_text: two, not a group acting [on another]; not a group [acting] on a group — the five are the owners of the <s>saṃghakarma</s> (community act). ||

body.translated_text: Not one [acting on] one,

body.text: buddho bhagavān caṇpāyāṃ viharati gargāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre / tena khalu samayena ṣaḍvargikā bhikṣava imāny evaṃrūpāṇy adharmakarmāṇi kurvanti / tadyathā eko 'py ekasya / eko dvayoḥ / ekaḥ saṃbahulānām* / dvāv api dvayoḥ / dvāv ekasya / dvau saṃbahulānām* / saṃbahulā api saṃbahulānām* / saṃbahulā ekasya / saṃbahulā dvayoḥ / (

children.text: ) gaṇo gaṇasya / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / bhagavān āha / tasmān naikenaikasya karma kartavyam* / naikena dvayoḥ / naikena saṃbahulānām* /
children.translated_text: a <s>gaṇa</s> (faction) on a <s>gaṇa</s>. The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Therefore, one should not perform an act on one person alone; nor one on two; nor one on a group;

children.text: dvābhyāṃ dvayoḥ / na dvābhyām ekasya / na dvābhyāṃ saṃbahulānām* / na saṃbahulaiḥ saṃbahulānām* / na saṃbahulair ekasya / na saṃbahulair dvayoḥ / na gaṇena gaṇasya / kurvanti / sātisāra bhavanti /
children.translated_text: two on two; nor two on one; nor two on a group; nor a group on a group; nor a group on one; nor a group on two; nor a faction on a faction. If they do, they commit a transgression."

body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, was dwelling at <s>Campā</s>, on the bank of <s>Gargā</s>'s lotus pond. At that time, the monks of the group of six performed these kinds of illegitimate acts: namely, one [acting] on one; one on two; one on a group; two on two; two on one; two on a group; a group on a group; a group on one; a group on two;

body.text: api tu bhikṣavaḥ paṃca saṃghakarmaṇāṃ svāminaḥ / katame paṃca / catvāro bhikṣavaḥ saṃghaḥ / pāṃcāpi bhikṣavaḥ saṃghaḥ / daśa bhikṣavaḥ
body.translated_text: "Rather, <s>bhikṣus</s>, there are five [quorums that are] the owners of the <s>saṃghakarma</s> (community act). Which five? Four <s>bhikṣus</s> [constitute] a <s>saṃgha</s>. Five <s>bhikṣus</s> also [constitute] a <s>saṃgha</s>. Ten <s>bhikṣus</s>

body.text: tatra bhikṣavo yatra catvāro bhikṣavaḥ prativasanti / arhati tatra saṃgho dharmeṇa sarvakarmāṇi kartum* / sthāpayitvā pāṃcānāṃ pravāraṇāṃ daśānām upasaṃpadaṃ viṃśatīnāṃ cāvarhaṇam* /
body.translated_text: Where four <s>bhikṣus</s> reside — there the <s>saṃgha</s> is competent to perform all actions (<s>karma</s>) in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, except for the <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony) requiring five, the <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination) requiring ten, and the <s>āvarhaṇa</s> (rehabilitation) requiring twenty.

body.text: yatra paṃca prativasanti / arhati tatra saṃgho dharmeṇa sarvakarmāṇi kartum* / sthāpayitvā daśānām upasaṃpadaṃ viṃśatīnāṃ cāvarhaṇam* /
body.translated_text: Where five reside — there the <s>saṃgha</s> is competent to perform all actions in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, except for the <s>upasaṃpad</s> (full ordination) requiring ten and the <s>āvarhaṇa</s> (rehabilitation) requiring twenty.

body.text: yatra daśa prativasanti / arhati tatra saṃghaḥ sarvakarmāṇi kartum* / sthāpayitvā viṃśatīnāṃ āvarhaṇam* /
body.translated_text: Where ten reside — there the <s>saṃgha</s> is competent to perform all actions, except for the <s>āvarhaṇa</s> (rehabilitation) requiring twenty.

body.text: yatra viṃśatir bhikṣavaḥ prativasanti uttare ca / arhati tatra saṃgho dharmeṇa sarvakarmāṇi kartum* /
body.translated_text: Where twenty <s>bhikṣus</s> or more reside — there the <s>saṃgha</s> is competent to perform all actions in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: uddānam* /
body.translated_text: <s>Uddāna</s> (summary verse):

children.translated_text: The action requiring a group of four, the individual, [and] the deficient one are set forth;
The fourfold <s>karma</s> (action) with one under probation (<s>pārivāsika</s>) as the fourth is not [rightly] remembered.

body.text: caturvargakaraṇīyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ karma ūnāś catvāraḥ kurvanti / adharmakarma ca tad avinayakarma ca / na tat tathā karaṇīyam* / saṃghaś ca tena sātisāraḥ / caturvargakaraṇīyaṃ karma āgārikacaturthāḥ kurvanti / adharmakarma ca tad avinayakarma ca / na ca tat tathā karaṇīyam* / saṃghaś ca tena sātisāraḥ / evaṃ śrāmaṇerakaḥ ṣaṇḍhapaṇḍakaḥ bhikṣuṇīdūṣako mātṛghātakaḥ pitṛghātakaḥ arhaghātakaḥ saṃghabhedakaḥ tathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādakas tīrthikas tīrthakāvakrāntikaḥ steyāsaṃvāsiko nānāsaṃvasiko 'saṃvāsikaḥ pārivāsikacaturthāḥ karma kurvanti / adharmakarma ca tad avinayakarma ca /

children.text: tat tathā karaṇīyam* / saṃghaś ca tena sātisāraḥ /
children.translated_text: not be so performed, and the <s>saṃgha</s> incurs a transgression thereby.

body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, when an action requiring a group of four is performed by [only] four who are deficient [in qualification], that is an unlawful action (<s>adharmakarma</s>) and an action contrary to discipline (<s>avinayakarma</s>); it should not be so performed, and the <s>saṃgha</s> incurs a transgression (<s>sātisāra</s>) thereby. When an action requiring a group of four is performed with a householder (<s>āgārika</s>) as the fourth, that is an unlawful action and an action contrary to discipline; it should not be so performed, and the <s>saṃgha</s> incurs a transgression thereby. Likewise [when performed with] a novice (<s>śrāmaṇeraka</s>), a eunuch (<s>ṣaṇḍha</s>), a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (sexually incapacitated person), one who has violated a nun (<s>bhikṣuṇīdūṣaka</s>), a matricide (<s>mātṛghātaka</s>), a patricide (<s>pitṛghātaka</s>), a slayer of an <s>Arhat</s> (<s>arhaghātaka</s>), a schismatic (<s>saṃghabhedaka</s>), one who with malicious intent has shed the blood of a <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>tathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarudhirotpādaka</s>), a non-Buddhist ascetic (<s>tīrthika</s>), one who has returned from a non-Buddhist order (<s>tīrthakāvakrāntika</s>), one who dwells by theft (<s>steyāsaṃvāsika</s>), one of different communion (<s>nānāsaṃvasika</s>), one expelled from communion (<s>asaṃvāsika</s>), [or] with one under probation (<s>pārivāsika</s>) as the fourth — [when they] perform the action, that is an unlawful action and an action contrary to discipline;

children.translated_text: Which [is the unlawful act]? When expulsion (<s>utsāraṇa</s>) has not been incurred, they expel one who has not incurred it. As the announcement (<s>anuśrāvaṇa</s>) for one being expelled should be, they do not so expel. [That is] an unlawful act. Which is the lawful act? When expulsion has been incurred, they expel one who has incurred it. As the announcement for one being expelled should be, they so expel. [That is] a lawful act. When reinstatement (<s>osāraṇa</s>) has not been merited, they reinstate one who has not merited it. As the announcement for one being reinstated should be, they do not so reinstate. [That is] an unlawful act. When reinstatement has been merited, they reinstate one who has merited it. As the announcement for one being reinstated should be, they so reinstate. [That is] a lawful act. An act requiring a motion (<s>jñaptikarma</s>) — they perform it without making the motion. [That is] an unlawful act. An act requiring a motion — they perform it having made the motion.

children.translated_text: [That is] a lawful act. An act with the motion as the second element (<s>jñaptidvitīya karma</s>) — they make the announcement once without making the motion. An act with the motion as the fourth element (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>) — they make the announcement three times without making the motion. [That is] an unlawful act. An act with the motion as the fourth element — they make the announcement three times having made the motion. [That is] a lawful act. children.translated_text: Discordant, concordant, they arise; by valid or invalid procedure one may suspend;
with reinstatement — these are the topics summarized in the <s>Karmavastu</s> (Section on Legal Procedures).

body.text: vyagrakarma / samagrakarma / vyagrakarma katamat* / yāvanto bhikṣavaḥ sīmāprāptāḥ kriyāprāptās te sarve samavahitāḥ saṃmukhībhūtāś chandārhebhyaś ca cchandenānītā bhavanti / samavahitāś ca bhikṣavaḥ saṃmukhībhūtāḥ prativahanti pratikrośanti / yeṣāṃ prativahatāṃ pratikrośatāṃ pratikrośo rohati / karmāṇi ca kurvanti / idam ucyate vyagrakarma / samagrakarma katamat* / yāvanto bhikṣavaḥ sīmāprāptāḥ kriyāprāptās te sarve samavahitāḥ saṃmukhībhūtāś chandārhebhyaś ca cchandenānītā bhavanti / samavahitāś ca bhikṣavaḥ saṃmukhībhūtā na prativahanti na pratikrośanti / yeṣāṃ prativahatāṃ pratikrośatāṃ pratikrośo rohati / karmāṇi ca kurvanti / idam ucyate samagrakarma /
body.translated_text: Discordant act. Concordant act. What is a discordant act? As many monks as have arrived within the <s>sīmā</s> (boundary) and are eligible to participate, all are attentive and present face-to-face, and proxies have been brought from those eligible for proxy. Yet the attentive monks who are present face-to-face protest and object. Those whose protest while protesting and objecting is sustained — and they perform legal acts. This is called a discordant act. What is a concordant act? As many monks as have arrived within the <s>sīmā</s> (boundary) and are eligible to participate, all are attentive and present face-to-face, and proxies have been brought from those eligible for proxy. The attentive monks who are present face-to-face do not protest and do not object. Those whose protest while protesting and objecting would be sustained — and they perform legal acts. This is called a concordant act.

body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>: "Venerable sir, for how many does a protest not succeed?" "For ten, <s>Upāli</s>: for one who is shameless, for one who has a hidden motive, for one who is foolish, for one who is confused, for one who is incompetent, for one who is unskilled, for one standing outside the <s>sīmā</s> (boundary), for one who has departed from proper deportment, for one whose speech is unrestrained." "Venerable sir, for how many does a protest succeed?" "For four, <s>Upāli</s>: for one in his natural state, for one standing within the <s>sīmā</s> (boundary), for one who has not departed from proper deportment, and for one whose speech is restrained." The venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>: "Venerable sir, how many acts of suspension are there?"
